summary.text: Geology is the natural science of Earth and other astronomical bodies, the rocks they are made of, and the processes that change them over time.
By studying rocks and their minerals, geologists piece together Earth's history, including its age, plate tectonics, past climates and the history of life.
It has practical uses too, from finding minerals, hydrocarbons and water to understanding natural hazards and fixing environmental problems.

items.prompt: Lava pours from a volcano, cools and hardens on the hillside. What type of rock has formed?
items.explain: Rock that solidifies from melt, such as magma or lava, is igneous rock.

items.prompt: Sand worn from old cliffs settles on a sea floor and, over ages, is buried and hardened into stone. What type of rock is it?
items.explain: Weathered and eroded rock that is redeposited and lithified becomes sedimentary rock, such as sandstone.

items.prompt: A layer of shale is buried deep and squeezed by great heat and pressure, but never melts. What does it become?
items.explain: Heat and pressure change the minerals of igneous and sedimentary rocks, turning them into metamorphic rock.

items.prompt: You rub an unknown mineral across a porcelain plate and note the color of the line it leaves. Which test is this?
items.explain: The streak test scratches a sample on porcelain, and the streak's color helps identify the mineral.

items.prompt: Two samples of the same mineral turn up in quite different colors. What is the likely reason?

options.label: One of them has been heated by acid
Color depends only on the sample's size

items.explain: Color is mostly diagnostic, but impurities can change a mineral's color.

items.prompt: Can a metamorphic rock ever end up as an igneous rock?

options.label: No, metamorphic rock is the final stage
Only if it first wears down into sediment
Yes, if it melts and then solidifies again
Only if it is buried under more sediment

items.explain: All three rock types can melt into new magma, from which igneous rock can solidify again.

pack.title: Rocks Remember Earth's Past
pack.question: How do rocks form, change and record Earth's history?

beats.title: Rocks Remember Earth's Past
beats.hook: Any of the three rock types can melt and later harden into a new rock.

beats.prompt: A sedimentary rock is buried so deep that it melts completely. When that melt cools and hardens, what rock forms?
beats.explain: Any rock type can melt into new magma, and rock that solidifies from melt is igneous.

choices.label: Sedimentary rock again
choices.feedback: Sedimentary rock forms from deposited particles, not from cooling melt.

choices.label: Metamorphic rock
choices.feedback: Metamorphic rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting; once melted, it is a new start.

beats.prompt: Sort each description into its rock type.
beats.explain: Igneous rock comes from melt, sedimentary rock from deposited particles, and metamorphic rock from heat and pressure changing existing rock.

beats.prompt: Match each mineral test to how it works.

right.label: How light reflects from the surface
Dripping acid to look for fizzing

beats.explain: Each test checks a different physical property that helps identify a mineral.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning about the rock cycle is wrong; which?

steps.text: Rocks are weathered and eroded into particles.
The particles are redeposited and lithified into sedimentary rock.
Heat and pressure can turn that rock into metamorphic rock.
Metamorphic rock can never melt, so the cycle ends there.

beats.explain: All three rock types can melt again, forming new magma from which igneous rock solidifies.

beats.idea: Rocks form, break down, transform and melt in a cycle, and studying them lets geologists reconstruct Earth's history.
